## What we want to discover {#next-questions}

![](media/prospects/discovery-map.svg){.slide-media .nostretch style="--media-max-height: 600px;" fig-alt="Open questions placed on a neutrino-energy axis from 1 TeV to 1 EeV over the measured cosmic neutrino spectrum: Seyfert galaxies beyond NGC 1068 at 1.5 to 15 TeV; the spectral break near 25 TeV, pp or p-gamma; the Milky Way and PeVatrons above 200 TeV; the neutrino cross section from Earth absorption above 40 TeV; the Glashow resonance at 6.3 PeV; and KM3-230213A at about 220 PeV, source or cosmogenic. Transients through alerts and new physics can appear at any energy."}

::: {.media-caption}
Questions on the energy axis · Spectrum: [IceCube (2026)](https://arxiv.org/abs/2507.22233v3) · [Glashow: IceCube (2021)](https://arxiv.org/abs/2110.15051) · [KM3-230213A: KM3NeT (2025)](https://doi.org/10.1038/s41586-024-08543-1)
:::

::: {.notes}
**Say:** Here is the wish list on one energy axis: which galaxies make most of the neutrinos, how bright our own Milky Way is, what makes the bend in the spectrum, what the very highest-energy neutrinos are — and, along the way, how neutrinos themselves interact.

Allow about 90 seconds; each item points back to a slide of this lecture.

1. Populations: decompose the diffuse flux. Seyfert galaxies beyond NGC 1068
(the bar is NGC 1068's well-constrained 1.5–15 TeV range,
[IceCube, arXiv:2510.13403](https://arxiv.org/abs/2510.13403); population
evidence in northern X-ray AGN and southern Seyferts) and radio-bright blazars
([Plavin et al., ApJ 894, 101 (2020)](https://arxiv.org/abs/2001.00930)).
2. A neutrino map of the Galaxy and LHAASO's PeVatrons: Baikal-GVD cascades above
200 TeV ([ApJ 982, 73 (2025)](https://arxiv.org/abs/2411.05608)), IceCube's
Galactic plane ([Science 380 (2023)](https://arxiv.org/abs/2307.04427)) and
LHAASO's diffuse and ultra-high-energy sources
([PRL 131, 151001 (2023)](https://arxiv.org/abs/2305.05372)).
3. The production zone, coronae or jets, and transients found through alerts
(slides on hidden sources and jets).
4. The break near 30 TeV (CF: $10^{4.39}$ GeV, Table III of
[PRL 136, 121002 (2026)](https://arxiv.org/abs/2507.22233v3)) and pp versus
p-gamma: the Glashow resonance at 6.3 PeV
([Nature 591, 220 (2021)](https://arxiv.org/abs/2110.15051)) and the flavour
composition test the target, since $\bar\nu_e$ yields differ between channels.
5. Events of order 100 PeV: KM3-230213A, median 220 PeV
([KM3NeT, Nature 638, 376 (2025)](https://doi.org/10.1038/s41586-024-08543-1)):
an extreme source or a cosmogenic neutrino from cosmic rays on background light.
6. The cross section at TeV–PeV energies from Earth absorption, back to slide 7:
IceCube measured it with upgoing muons; absorption is expected above 40 TeV
([Nature 551, 596 (2017)](https://arxiv.org/abs/1711.08119)). Deviations would be
signs of physics beyond the Standard Model, as could anomalous flavour ratios.

Label heights on the figure are arbitrary; only the cyan band has a flux scale.
Positions are published values, not forecasts. Generator: `assets/prospects/`.

## What we lack {#what-we-need}

:::::: {.panel-tabset}

### Instruments and analysis

| What is missing | Why it matters |
|:---|:---|
| Northern exposure beyond $10\,\mathrm{km}^3$ | Faint sources and the Galactic Centre seen through the Earth |
| Sharper cascade directions | All flavours point back to sources |
| More events above $1\,\mathrm{PeV}$ | The spectrum's end, Glashow events, the 100 PeV puzzle |
| Global alerts, joint analyses, open data | One sky, several telescopes |
| Calibrated optics of water and ice | Energies and directions we can trust |
| Population theory within the gamma-ray budget | Turning many faint hints into sources |

### People

![](media/prospects/people-chain.svg){.slide-media .nostretch style="--media-width: 1450px; --media-max-height: 420px;" fig-alt="Symbolic chain: the programme ФНАФЧ, neutrino physics and particle astrophysics, with courses, seminars and the Baikal school; people, students who become researchers and lecturers; results, data analysis, for example the Milky Way in Baikal-GVD data with a first author from the programme; and the next experiment, B-HUNT, Russia and China."}

**Telescopes are built and understood by people.**

::: {.media-caption}
ФНАФЧ — Физика нейтрино и астрофизика частиц · [Courses on teach-in.ru](https://teach-in.ru/course?tags=ФНАФЧ)
:::

::::::

::: {.notes}
**Say:** To get there we need bigger and sharper telescopes in the north, a network that shares alerts and data, careful calibration, theory that adds everything up — and, above all, people: the students we teach today will analyse B-HUNT data tomorrow.

Allow about 90 seconds. Instruments and analysis: the 10-cubic-kilometre scale
is the regime of the proposed next-generation arrays (IceCube-Gen2 optical array
8 km³, NEON 10 km³, TRIDENT 7.5 km³, HUNT ~30 km³; observatory slide). Northern
sites see the Galactic Centre through the Earth. Cascade directions matter because
cascades carry all flavours and the best energy measurement. Above 1 PeV only a
handful of events are known so far. Alerts and joint
analyses combine telescopes at different latitudes (joint search tab); open data
make independent tests possible. Optical calibration of the medium controls energy
and direction systematics (source-sensitivity slide). Population models must not
overshoot the gamma-ray background (gamma-budget slide; Groth and Ahlers,
PRD 111, 103052 (2025)).

People. ФНАФЧ stands for «Физика нейтрино и астрофизика частиц»; its courses are
on [teach-in.ru](https://teach-in.ru/course?tags=ФНАФЧ). D. V. Naumov has given
lecture courses on quantum field theory, the Standard Model, renormalization,
statistical data analysis and neutrino physics; courses on particle physics,
neutrino oscillations and numerical methods are planned. V. A. Allakhverdyan,
D. V. Naumov's student, solves problems and leads the seminars. Further courses
include Physical modelling (A. S. Sheshukov), particle astrophysics seminars
(A. M. Libanov), general relativity, and the Baikal International Summer School
on Physics of Elementary Particles and Astrophysics. Allakhverdyan and Sheshukov
are D. V. Naumov's students who now teach in the programme. Allakhverdyan is the
first author of the Baikal-GVD Galactic-plane analysis
([ApJ 982, 73 (2025)](https://arxiv.org/abs/2411.05608)) and of the Earth-transmission
figure on slide 7. This is the chain the figure shows: programme → people →
results → B-HUNT.

## Where are the sources? {#conclusions}

::::: {.columns}
::: {.column width="66%"}
![](media/prospects/sources-sky.svg){.slide-media .nostretch style="--media-max-height: 560px;" fig-alt="Equatorial sky map. The Galactic plane with the Galactic Centre is marked as diffuse neutrino emission from the Milky Way. NGC 1068 stands for Seyfert galaxies, TXS 0506+056 for blazars, and an open circle marks the direction of KM3-230213A, whose origin is open. Caption: most of the flux comes from many faint sources, not yet resolved."}
:::
::: {.column width="31%"}
**Found:** our Galaxy · NGC 1068 and Seyfert galaxies · blazar candidates.

**Still open:** most of the flux — a crowd of faint sources.

**Next:** bigger telescopes and networks — B-HUNT, KM3NeT, IceCube-Gen2.
:::
:::::

::: {.question}
We have found where to look. Next we must resolve the crowd.
:::

::: {.media-caption}
Positions: [Baikal-GVD source list (2026)](https://arxiv.org/abs/2603.21261v2) · Evidence: result slides of this lecture
:::

::: {.notes}
**Say:** We started by asking where the sources are. Today we can point to a few: our own Milky Way, the active galaxy NGC 1068 and its Seyfert relatives, and blazars like TXS 0506+056 — but most of the neutrinos still come from a crowd of faint sources that only bigger telescopes, like B-HUNT in Baikal, will resolve.

Spend the final two minutes. This answers the question on slide 2, "We have
discovered the flux. Where are the sources?"

Found, with the strength stated on the result slides: diffuse Galactic emission
(IceCube 2023, 4.5 sigma; Baikal-GVD above 200 TeV, p = 1.4e-2, combined with
IceCube p = 3.4e-4); NGC 1068 (IceCube, 4.0 sigma in the 2026 catalogue analysis)
and population evidence from X-ray-bright Seyfert galaxies (3.3 sigma northern
ensemble, 3.0 sigma southern stacking); blazars as candidates (TXS 0506+056:
the 2017 alert association at about 3 sigma and the archival flare at 3.5 sigma;
radio-bright blazars with post-trial p = 2e-3). KM3-230213A has no identified
counterpart. The map marks positions from the Baikal-GVD source list
(arXiv:2603.21261v2, Table 1); it shows no fluxes or significances and does not
draw the individual population members.

Still open: the diffuse flux is far brighter than the identified sources
(IceCube PRL 136, 121002 (2026), Fig. 3; population constraints, Groth and Ahlers
2025), so most of it comes from many individually faint emitters. Their classes,
production zones (coronae or jets) and the origin of the spectral break remain
to be measured. Next: exposure, angular resolution, calibration and networks
(previous slide), with B-HUNT, KM3NeT and IceCube-Gen2. These are routes, not
guaranteed discoveries.
